review_notes:
I reviewed all 82 lines. I also read the supporting definitions in NormalizedPoisson.lean (`normalizedPoisson` and `exists_complex_poisson`), RealSobolev.lean (`RealSmooth.ofReal` and `source`), AnalyticSupport.lean (the `SmoothRealFunction` structure), GlobalPartition.lean (`Smooth.ofReal`) and ComplexOperator.lean (`complexL`).

Each lemma looks appropriately general.
- `ext_value` is a structure extensionality lemma. Its only fields are `value` and `smooth`, and `smooth` is a proposition.
- `laplacian_constant` is stated for an arbitrary Kähler metric and an arbitrary real constant.
- `complexL_ofReal` is stated for any `SmoothRealFunction`.
- `exists_real_smooth_poisson` needs `[T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X]`. These are exactly the hypotheses of `normalizedPoisson`, which it calls. Connectedness is needed because the kernel of the Laplacian is the constants. Dropping any of them would need new mathematics.

All the types are bespoke (`ComplexAtlas`, `SmoothRealFunction`), so there is no scalar type to generalise to a field class.

I found no useful generalisation I could justify from the sources I read. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not search for other uses of these lemmas.
